rejected_candidates.reason: On the pinned evaluator interpreter (CPython 3.12) the only observable difference is the presence of a __partialmethod__ attribute that CPython 3.13 requires; a contract would check that an identifier was chosen rather than that a behavior was built.

The numeric results of the affected timestamp conversion are identical on both endpoints; the only observable signal is a DeprecationWarning emitted at module import on Python >= 3.12, whose text is owned by the interpreter. Held in reserve.
Removal of dead Python 2 compatibility aliases. Probed Bits construction, urlutils text coercion, timeutils.total_seconds and deprutils module typing: identical on both endpoints.
Qualifies as a contract, but it extends the same nested-search surface already covered by the selected iteration_tools demand (pr_394) and would duplicate it. Held in reserve.
Docstring-only fix (module name in an example); no observable behavior change.

Adds a brand-new public helper (file rotation). A contract could only assert that a specific new public name exists, which the authoring standard restricts to demands that spell the interface out; the window supplies enough pure-behavior candidates without it. Held in reserve.

Mostly CI, packaging and docs. The library-visible remainder is the disappearance of DeprecationWarning from relative_time / decimal_relative_time / ecoutils import on Python >= 3.12, which is interpreter-version dependent rather than a contracted behavior. Held in reserve.
The source change is a new public backport of str.removeprefix; its behavior is already that of the standard library method, so a contract would only test that the name exists.
Adds fsync before closing the temporary file in atomic saves. A durability guarantee with no difference observable from inside the process.
Adds a brand-new public list-formatting function. A contract would reduce to asserting the new name plus one exact formatting convention. Held in reserve.
Adds a brand-new public run-once decorator; same objection as pr_388 - the contract would be a name check plus a call counter. Held in reserve.
Docstring-only addition to the run-once decorator; no observable behavior change.
Export-list bookkeeping for the function added by pr_388; contracting it would test the __all__ contents, i.e. naming.
Fixes a syntax error inside a docstring example; no observable behavior change.
CI modernization, OIDC publishing and a release skill file; no library behavior in the window's import surface.
Removes an unused local in the chunked-list rebalance path; probed identical on both endpoints.

Qualifies as a contract (the starter raises IndexError where a plain list clamps to the front), but shares the list_containers family and the same 60k-element setup as the selected pr_389 demand. Held in reserve.

A performance change. Its only observable behavior difference is that a search pattern able to match the empty string stops raising IndexError, which is incidental to the change's intent and would misdescribe the upstream work. Held in reserve.
